data.body_html:
Choosing between the Mangusta 80 and the Azimut 58 Flybridge for your Marbella yacht charter can feel like splitting hairs—both are premium vessels departing from Puerto Banús, both carry up to 12 guests, and both come with a licensed skipper and full amenities. But the devil is in the details: speed, deck layout, price structure, and the all-important free jet ski on the Mangusta. This comparison breaks down every key difference so you can book the right boat for your Costa del Sol adventure. For a broader look at our fleet, visit our [main charter page](/).

Size and Layout: Mangusta 80 vs Azimut 58

The Mangusta 80 measures 24 metres (78.7 ft) and is built for performance, with a sleek, sporty profile and a large aft sunpad that converts into a lounging area. Its open-plan main deck prioritises socialising around the central bar and seating. The Azimut 58 Flybridge, at 17.6 metres (57.7 ft), is shorter but compensates with a spacious flybridge deck that offers panoramic views of the Marbella coastline—perfect for sunset cruises. Both yachts have a beam of around 5 metres, but the Azimut feels more voluminous thanks to its raised helm station and multiple seating zones.

Speed and Performance

The Mangusta 80 is a thoroughbred, with twin MTU engines pushing it to a top speed of 35 knots and a cruising speed of 28 knots. It’s ideal for guests who want to cover distance quickly—say, a day trip to Sotogrande or Estepona. The Azimut 58 Flybridge, powered by MAN engines, cruises at 22–25 knots and tops out around 30 knots. It’s smoother and more fuel-efficient, making it better for relaxed cruising along the Golden Mile or anchoring at Cala Cortés. If speed is your priority, the Mangusta wins.

Capacity and Comfort

Both yachts officially carry 12 passengers, but the experience differs. The Mangusta 80 feels more exclusive and sporty, with a focus on forward-facing sunpads and a central cockpit. The Azimut 58 offers a flybridge with a second helm, a wet bar, and ample shade—ideal for larger groups who want to spread out. For families or corporate groups, the Azimut’s layout is more versatile. The Mangusta suits couples or groups who want a faster, more adrenaline-filled day.

Price and Inclusions

The Mangusta 80 is priced at a fixed €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter, and that includes a free jet ski—a major perk for water sports enthusiasts. The Azimut 58 Flybridge is priced on request, meaning you can negotiate shorter or longer charters. Both include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and 21% IVA. For a fixed-price deal with a jet ski, the Mangusta offers clear value. For flexibility, the Azimut wins.

Best Use Cases

  • Mangusta 80: Speed demons, jet ski lovers, day trips to Estepona or Sotogrande, bachelor parties, adrenaline seekers.
  • Azimut 58 Flybridge: Families, corporate events, sunset cruises, relaxed anchoring at Cabopino, groups wanting panoramic views.

Which One Should You Book?

If you want to feel the wind in your hair and have a jet ski at your disposal, go with the Mangusta 80. If you prefer lounging on a flybridge with a glass of cava while watching the sun dip behind La Concha, the Azimut 58 is your match. Both yachts deliver an unforgettable day on the Mediterranean. For more options, browse our [full fleet](/).

Frequently asked questions

How do the speeds of the Mangusta 80 and Azimut 58 compare?

The Mangusta 80 is a performance yacht with a top speed of around 35 knots, making it one of the fastest in its class. The Azimut 58 Flybridge cruises comfortably at 22–25 knots, prioritising stability and fuel efficiency over outright speed.

Which yacht has more space for parties?

Both yachts accommodate up to 12 passengers, but the Azimut 58 offers a larger flybridge and more deck lounging areas, ideal for socialising. The Mangusta 80 has a sleek, sportier layout with a spacious main deck and a large sunpad aft.

What is included in the charter price for each yacht?

The Mangusta 80 charter at €4,719 (minimum 4 hours) includes a free jet ski, licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and IVA. The Azimut 58 pricing is on request but includes the same amenities.

Can I charter the Azimut 58 for a shorter trip?

Yes, the Azimut 58 can be chartered for shorter durations, but pricing is on request. Contact us via WhatsApp for a custom quote. The Mangusta 80 requires a minimum 4-hour charter.

Which yacht is better for a family day out?

The Azimut 58 Flybridge is more family-friendly, with a stable ride, shaded flybridge, and multiple seating areas. The Mangusta 80 suits thrill-seeking families who want speed and jet ski fun.

Do both yachts depart from Puerto Banús?

Yes, both the Mangusta 80 and Azimut 58 depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella. This allows easy access to hotspots like Cabopino, Cala del Faro, and Estepona.

Which yacht offers better value for money?

The Mangusta 80 offers clear value with its fixed 4-hour price including a jet ski. The Azimut 58’s price is negotiable per hour, so for longer charters it may be more cost-effective. Compare based on your group size and desired activities.

Can I bring my own food and drinks?

Yes, you can bring additional food and drinks aboard both yachts. The standard package includes soft drinks, beer, wine, cava, and light snacks. The skipper will handle all catering logistics.
